# Tlāltēcuhtli, spelled the way the sources wrote it
There is a version of this name the early internet had to settle for: *tlaltecuhtli*. This is the file on how **Tlāltēcuhtli** replaced it.

Tlāltēcuhtli appears in several Mesoamerican creation accounts as the earth monster who must be defeated and dismembered before the present world can exist. The most detailed Nahuatl version is the Histoyre du Méchique, in which Quetzalcōātl and Tēzcatlīpōca split the earth monster in two; the K'iche' Maya Popol Vuh preserves a cognate tradition. In the Nahua cosmogony preserved by colonial sources, the gods created the present earth from the body of a great monster.  In some versions Quetzalcōātl and Tēzcatlīpōca seized Tlāltēcuhtli or a crocodilian earth-being and tore it in two: one half became the sky, the other the earth.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Tlāltēcuhtli
- **ASCII form:** tlaltecuhtli
- **Meaning:** "Lord of the earth"
- **Domain of influence:** Earth
- **Pantheon:** Nahuatl
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** —
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 245 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

Strip **Tlāltēcuhtli** to *tlaltecuhtli* and 2 pieces of evidence vanish:

- **a → ā** — Long vowel: the vowel length the ASCII form cannot show.
- **e → ē** — Long vowel: the vowel length the ASCII form cannot show.

A reader who knows the marks hears the name correctly on the first try. A reader who never sees them never gets the chance.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Tlāltēcuhtli** lives at [/sites/tlaltecuhtli/](/sites/tlaltecuhtli/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/tlaltecuhtli/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/tlaltecuhtli/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/tlaltecuhtli/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Tlāltēcuhtli** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Agriculture, Food & Harvest** — The earth lord who must be fed to give food.
- **Environmental & Climate Services** — The earth as a living being demanding balance.
- **Mining & Natural Resources** — The earth lord whose body holds the ores.

The mapping is conservative on purpose: only resonances that can be argued aloud. The rest of the atlas follows the same rule, industry by industry.
